hypothesis: Shorter recency may help established/high-support players adapt faster, while the incumbent 730-day half-life may better stabilize sparse-history players.
outcome: exact full-I2 log-loss difference: LL_365 - LL_730; negative favors 365

support_definition.direct_model_support: For each monthly direct-I2 model, use its training data only and count exponentially unweighted historical I2 PA observations for the 18 scheduled hitters and both scheduled starting pitchers appearing in the game.
summaries: minimum hitter support across 18 scheduled hitters
median hitter support across 18 scheduled hitters
minimum starter-pitcher support across the two starters
median support across all 20 direct-model identities
support_definition.reason: Test the user's sparse-history concern directly rather than using career age or service time as a proxy.

diagnostics: per-season Spearman association between support summaries and LL_365 - LL_730
precommitted support quartiles derived within each season from pregame support only
mean and paired-date clustered uncertainty of LL_365 - LL_730 within support quartiles
pooled 2022-2025 interaction direction with season fixed effects
advance_rule: Advance to Phase 32B adaptive-rule design only if higher-support strata favor 365 relative to lower-support strata in at least 3 of 4 development seasons and the pooled interaction has the same direction. Otherwise reject support-adaptive recency without using 2026.
replication_rule: 2026 is consulted only after a specific adaptive rule is frozen in Phase 32B.
